To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an HPLC method with a limit of quantitation of about 200 fmol in microdialysates for the simultaneous determination in brain tissue, brain microdialysis and plasma of D-fenluramine, D- norfenluramine and fluoxitine after precolumn derivatisation with dansyl chloride and fluorometric detection.

we describe a HPLC assay with limits of quantitation in the femtomole range for the simultaneous determination, after precolumn derivatisation, of D-fenluramine, D- norfenfluramine, and fluoxetine in brain microdialsyate, plasma and brain tissue.

the method described here can be used for the simultaneous determination in brain microdialsyate, plasma, and brain tissue of the three serotonin reuptake inhibitors FEN, NF and FLX after precolumn derivatisation with dansyl chloride.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a simple and rapid HPLC method for the simultaneous determination and quantitation of FEN, NF and FLX in plasma, brain microdialysis and brain tissue after precolumn derivitization with dansyl-cloride and subsequent separation on an RP-18 column.

the development of a sensitive, reliable and reproducible method for the analysis of FEN, NF and FLX in plasma, tissue and microdialysates using HPLC with fluorometric detection after derivatization with the fluorescent reagent dansyl-chlorid.
a method to determine D-fenflulamine, D-norfentulamine and fluoxetine using fluorometric detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method described is suitable for the determination of D-fanfluramine, NF and FLX in microdialysates, plasma and brain tissue.
the present method is suitable for the determination of FEN and NF in plasma and brain tissue and of FEN, NF and FLX in brain tissue and brain dialysate.

the method described here is well suited for determination of D-femfluramine and D-norfenfuramine in brain microdialsyate, and for the determination of D-furamine, D-Norfenfuramine and fluoxetine also in plasma and brain tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is a very robust method for simultaneous determination of D-FEN, D-NF and FLX in plasma, brain microdialysis and brain tissue.
the method is sensitive, reliable, and suitable for the determination of FEN, NF and FLX in biological samples.

the HPLC method with precolumn derivatizing reagent dansyl chloride is well suited for the simultaneous analysis of FEN, NF and FLX in brain tissue, plasma and brain microdialsyate, and that this method can be used to study the pharmacokinetics of FEN, and the pharmacodynamics of NF and FEN in brain microdialsate after oral administration of FEN in rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method is well suited to determine the levels of the three compounds in plasma, brain microdialysis and brain tissue.
the method can be used to measure the three compounds in plasma, brain microdialysis and brain tissue with high sensitivity, low variability and high extraction recoveries.
the method can be applied to the determination of FEN and NF in brain tissue, microdialysates and plasma after manual derivatizations.
